title: A reactivation order and deemed-work remedy can leave payment and later access unobserved
source_unit: One adjudicated Fair Work Commission platform-worker case, UDE2025/134
geography: Australia; comparative case used to test platform remedy and recovery stages in the US-centered atlas

observations.method: Case-level extraction from the official Fair Work Commission merits decision and reactivation order.
observations.uncertainty: The public record does not quantify lost pay, establish actual account restoration, or observe later work, substitute work, payment, or household recovery.
observations.subgroup: One named worker with adjudicated platform deactivation.
observations.counterinterpretation: Deemed work is a legal remedy construct, not proof of performed work, received wages, restored access, or equivalent future opportunity.

lost_pay_confer_direction.unit: parties directed to confer and report by 2025-11-07

quantified_lost_pay_order.unit: quantified payment orders in the checked public record

observations.method: Case-level extraction from the official order and bulletin; a direction to confer is kept separate from an amount, payment obligation, or receipt.
observations.uncertainty: A conference direction does not establish agreement, final quantum, payment, account status, or later work.
observations.subgroup: Same named worker case after reactivation order.
observations.counterinterpretation: A procedural remedy can move the case toward monetary resolution without producing a public payment or recovery outcome.

denominator.unit: named worker case and official search route

continued_work_or_switching_observed.unit: public later-work or switching records located

observations.method: Targeted official Fair Work Commission search across the merits decision, order, bulletin, and decisions/orders route; non-observation is not coded as private non-occurrence.
observations.uncertainty: Public search cannot establish private agreement, payment, account restoration, continued work, switching, or exit.
observations.subgroup: Same named worker case after the lost-pay conference direction.
observations.counterinterpretation: The case advances reactivation and legal remedy architecture but leaves payment, durability, trust, and practical exit open.

related_sources.claim: Bounded machine recheck preserving reactivation, deemed work, conference, payment, access, and later-work fields.
Official bulletin summary of reactivation and lost-pay conference stage.

boundary: This is one comparative Australian adjudicated case, not a worker prevalence estimate or a US population result. It distinguishes reactivation, deemed work, procedural lost-pay resolution, quantified payment, receipt, actual access, continued work, and practical exit.
